scope: Read-only audit of partner source, replay-state reconstruction and prior native API. No new matches or policy execution. Four recent it20 map identities excluded by preregistration before opening any archived trajectory; their game outputs were not read and are absent here.

stateful_policy_contract.inputs: One acting-seat public observation on each actual board transition. Feat.observe updates own viewpoint history; carry/replay on the common prefix even if the new expert has not yet acted. One observer advance per frame.
stateful_policy_contract.decode: Per-turn two complete token/context encodings, same shared selected prefix for recurrent heads, masks and joint budget. style=2; masked 0.75 partner + 0.25 Sapling logits. Per-slot decoder hidden state and prefix built afresh per turn. The return adjustment and protected roles/conflict rollback remain active. _HYBRID declares guard=false/search=false; this does not disable the return correction.
stateful_policy_contract.exact_difference: Only embedded expert payload and displayed expert name differ across the two frozen composite scripts, as validated by canonical AST equality after replacing those fields; identical quantized Sapling payload and return logic.
stateful_policy_contract.no_feature_leak: No hidden board state, opponent observation, source actions from current turn or future, or map identifier is needed by an acting policy. Here both masked seat hashes and simulator hash are for offline verification.

historical_partner_command_evidence.interpretation: Same historical public observation. switch = full it20 composite vs it50 composite; student = difference from the it20 composite with student coefficient zero. These are legal command differences, not paired terminal returns.

archive.scope: Pre-existing v1 vs original, four selected historical tree exercise roots per terrain. Completed original responses hold actor fixed after a single focal root intervention. These are known development/training cases; no winner or score is used as input here.

state_and_api.contract: Recreate the original game configuration/seed; check all 225 initial cell values by digest; authoritative official env advances on the common submitted simultaneous commands. Acting-seat carbon is masked separately for each seat.

At root t, one recorded common enemy joint action. Build opponent BeliefTracker by step and set_actions on its own masked historical views and committed commands; restore previous players; branch starts its own prebound MT19937 state and warm search costs. Each t+1..terminal calls full original agent again, no enemy tape replay as continuation. 64 trees have digested shared-state files and verified complete receipts. Under this protocol root action edit is only one named worker. Post-root own agent on BOTH arms stays fixed; neither arm tests a phase-dependent partner.

Pre-identity-checked source, public views, full root pronouncements and edit validation. Branch step records explicit native search issue/response, clock cost/RNG, public view hash, and action tape. Designed for one preselected root, guarded one-focal edits and then the frozen actor. Fixed-root common enemy command cannot read our alternative.

Full-game resumable runner. Bound candidate/parent plus opponent plus harness/weight identity, independent original entropy per new game, preserve completed rather than rerun. Committed opponent history reconstructs tr,prev; terminal native snapshot hash checked. Restores last committed MT19937 internal state and four _S_COST plus _S_STATS. Resume candidate by replay and verify each historical joint; a phase controller must reconstruct its own counter/timers from history or signed snapshot, otherwise refuse resume.

limits: Archived committed-action tapes with seed maps regenerate true terrain and both masked histories. They do not record original-vs-origin RNG at every arbitrary root. Shared branch initialization is a paired new stream; simulations with unseeded original and a wall-clock search are not guaranteed bit-identical across runs.

No archived paired terminal return for sustained it50 versus it20 phase switches was found within the certified 64-root cohort. It cannot be recovered by mixing earnings across different games or splicing future commands; both policies must be carried after the branch and the original examiner must actually respond.
Do not treat inherited root responses as claimed gains for a new partner controller or the 16 already exposed maps as a formal holdout.
